input.title: Verify in production: the re-opened withhold lane converges members without regression
input.body:
Original-issue: #1509
In-production-when: at least one member other than the canon stamps `claudinite-lifecycle` at `60831.1` or higher in its `.claudinite-settings.json` (`packs[]` entry `version`, read through `engine/installed-versions.mjs` — it is a per-entry stamp, not a central map).
Verify: For every member at `claudinite-lifecycle` >= 60831.1 — (a) its most recent Claudinite update run concluded `success`, not failure, and (b) `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` is absent or empty on its default branch. PASS = both, for every such member. FAIL = any failed update run since it took the version, or any file sitting in `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` — nothing declares a workflow materialization yet, so anything staged is the flow staging something it should not.
Not-before: 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day
Model: sonnet

## Why this could not be watched now

#1511 changed three things inside the flow **every member runs on every nightly converge**:

- `write` now stages a path under `.github/workflows/` instead of dropping it.
- The flow announces `CLAUDINITE_CAN_WITHHOLD_WORKFLOWS`, so records naming a workflow path stop skipping themselves.
- The staging sweep is scoped to files the current run did not stage, where it previously cleared the directory unconditionally.

The unit tests prove each in isolation against a synthetic member tree. What they cannot prove is that a real member — with its own declaration, its own pack set, its own drift — still converges green through the changed flow. `pack-update.mjs` is vendored verbatim, so a regression here is a regression on all 13 at once, and the failure would look like members quietly falling behind rather than anything red here.

The second half of `Verify:` is the sharper one. **Nothing currently materializes or rewrites a workflow path** — the record that will is deliberately held back (see #1509's tail, and the follow-up issue). So the correct observation today is that the lane is open and *idle*: any file appearing under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` means the flow is staging something no record asked for, which would be a defect in the `write` change rather than a delivery.

## Instructions to the run

1. Read `In-production-when:` against members' real `.claudinite-settings.json` on their default branches. Never infer it from a merge or from elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`.
   - Passes: comment the members checked and the version each stamps, and close this issue as completed.
   - Fails: reopen #1509 with a comment naming the member, what failed (the run id, or the staged path), and close this issue as completed.
3. **Not yet live** → set `Not-before:` to the instant you are reading this at plus `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment.

Every member holds the reader as of `claudinite-tasks` 60831.3, and **not one holds the line** — because nothing delivers `.github/workflows/` any more.

## The premise that closed the lane is now false

The withhold-and-hand-to-the-agent path shipped in #649 and worked. `packs/claudinite-canary-repo/migrations/2026-08-14-workflow-probe-current/` is documented as *"the first record to materialize into `.github/workflows/`"*.

#1317 closed it on one stated ground, at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs:238`:

> Nothing needs to: a member's workflows are static after adoption (#1317).

That was true when it was written. #1494 is the counterexample: a workflow change every member needs, with no route to them. The alternative on the table was 13 hand-opened PRs — which the canon's own standing decision rejects, because per-repo manual work reliably does not happen.

## What is actually still there

The lane was **emptied, not removed** — the `updates/*` convention, and exactly the reason it exists. All four seams survive:

| Seam | State |
|---|---|
| `registry.mjs` `WITHHOLD_CAPABLE_ENV` / `WORKFLOW_DEST` / skip-with-note | intact, live |
| `pack-update.mjs` `PENDING_DIR`, `stagedAt()` | emptied, addressable |
| `stagedFiles()` | live — the sweep uses it |
| `applyStageFor(specs, withheld)` | still takes and renders `withheld` |

What #1317 removed is four lines: `write` drops workflow paths (`:239`), `env: {}` makes the handshake permanently false (`:242`), the sweep deletes anything staged (`:266`), and `withheld` is hardcoded `[]` (`:311`).

**The credential question is settled.** The Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never push under `.github/workflows/` — that part of the doctrine is real, and GitHub rejects the whole ref, so writing one into a tree about to be pushed fails the entire converge. But the apply stage does not run on that token: it raises a work item for an agent session, and the Claude GitHub App carries `workflows: write`. That is what closes the loop, and it is why staging + apply-stage is the shape rather than a direct write.

## A false green found on the way

`applyMaterializations` guards workflow dests and reports `SKIPPED …(workflow file; this caller cannot deliver one)`. `applyRewrites` (`registry.mjs:140-155`) has no such guard:

```js
if (next !== text) { await write(file, next); done.push(file); }
```

`write` silently drops workflow paths, but `done.push(file)` runs regardless — so **a rewrite record targeting a workflow file reports success while writing nothing.** Nothing has hit it because no record rewrites a workflow yet; this change makes that the exact shape needed, so it must be fixed here. Two structurally-identical surfaces, one guarded.

## The work

1. `applyRewrites` gets the same guard and the same skip-with-note as `applyMaterializations`.
2. `pack-update.mjs` refills the four seams: stage workflow paths under `PENDING_DIR`, announce the handshake, collect the real `withheld`, and scope the sweep so it clears pre-existing staged files without deleting what this run just staged.
3. A `claudinite-tasks` migration record rewriting the executor to insert the `CLAUDINITE_VARS` line — a **rewrite**, not a materialize, so each member's own stamped `# claudinite:secrets` names survive. It carries `applyStage` so a session delivers the staged file.
4. Forced fleet delivery afterwards, since this is an engine-flow change.

{"id":5298546257,"number":1492,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"The executor carries repo variables as one `toJSON(vars)` bag","body":"A task that needs a repository **variable** today pays what a task needing a **secret** pays: the executor workflow must name it statically, `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot write, so a new value needs a human-merged PR in every member — the coupling that wedged one in #1296.

For secrets that cost was taken back deliberately in #1336/#1337, because the one-line alternative, `toJSON(secrets)`, is the shape GitHub's [malicious-workflow detection](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-28-github-actions-holds-potentially-malicious-workflows-for-approval/) flags: every run parks with zero jobs until a person clicks Approve, silently.

**That reasoning does not carry to `vars`.**

- The safeguard's stated threat model is credential theft. `vars` is the context GitHub's own docs define as non-sensitive — *"Variables provide a way to store and reuse non-sensitive configuration information […] By default, variables render unmasked in your build outputs. If you need greater security for sensitive information, such as passwords, use secrets instead."* Dumping a context GitHub already renders unmasked in logs is not an exfiltration signal.
- `${{ toJSON(vars) }}` is a mainstream pattern with Marketplace actions built to consume it. Flagging it would be a mass false-positive event.
- **We already field it.** `packs/static-website/stubs/workflows/static-site-ci.yml:62` and `static-site-deploy-pages.yml:70` both pass `REPO_VARS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}`, and have since before the safeguard shipped. No park. `read-config.mjs:41` already states the reasoning: *"`toJSON(vars)`, a context that structurally cannot carry a secret."*

## The change

One static line in the executor's work step, never regenerated, never a function of the task set:

```yaml
CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
```

- A reader beside `secrets-bag.mjs`, sharing its bag mechanics rather than copying them, with the same fall-back-to-plain-env posture that makes the pre-PR window uneventful.
- `taskEnv` unpacks it, so a task's code-work reads `process.env.<NAME>` for any repo variable with nothing naming it in YAML. Unlike the secrets bag there is no per-task selection: vars are non-sensitive by construction, so the blast-radius argument that justified `required_secrets` has nothing to bite on.
- The scheduler stub is untouched. It runs no task code, and its one named variable is the operator hold, which every entry point must read before any bag exists.
- The `toJSON(secrets)` guard stays exactly as strict, and gains a sibling asserting the vars line IS present.

## Caveat carried in the code, not just here

GitHub publishes no detection signals, thresholds or false-positive rate. This is inference from the threat model, the docs and our own field evidence — not a guarantee. If it ever did fire, the failure mode is the silent `action_required` park that cost a mis-diagnosis in #1330.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

    A rewrite record inserting the CLAUDINITE_VARS block into a member's live

## Three decisions worth reviewing **A rewrite, not a materialize.** The executor is not identical across members — the wiring converge stamps each one's own `required_secrets` beneath the `# claudinite:secrets` marker. The first asserts what the record *leaves alone*: the member's own `MEMBER_ONLY_TOKEN`, the marker, the bag landing above it, and a second `appliesTo` returning false. The second is a drift guard — it pins every line of the record's inserted block against the stub's own text, so an adopter and an upgrader cannot end up with different executors. Nothing else compares those two. I mutated one word of the record and watched it fail (`stub is missing the record's line: … vars-bag.mjs is the READER.`) before restoring.
